summary: Invoice shows reserve credit for unused reserved hours and missing per-minute burst charges after batch embedding run
description: Issue summary: Customer QuantaHealth reports that their February invoice includes a large reserve credit line for 120 reserved GPU-hours that were never consumed, while at the same time per-minute burst consumption from a large overnight batch embedding job (Feb 02 00:00 - 03:30 UTC) is missing entirely. Impact: Customer is seeing a credit reducing their invoice by ~$6,400 that they did not expect, and the missing burst charges cause incorrect cost attribution and make their internal cost center reconciliation impossible. Environment: Dedicated reservation (reserved-pool-phi-2), batch embedding job initiated via batch API, prod (us-east-1).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer ran a scheduled batch embedding job via the Batch API on 2026-02-02 00:10 UTC targeting model 'embed-multilingual-1' using dedicated pool 'reserved-pool-phi-2'.
2) Job completed successfully with expected token/embedding counts (customer provided job manifest and success status).
3) On 2026-02-03 customer noticed reserve credits applied on invoice line item 'Reserved capacity adjustment' for 120 hours dated 2026-02-01 to 2026-02-02 with reason 'unused reservation rollover'.
4) Customer expected per-minute burst usage lines for 2026-02-02 00:10–03:30 to appear under 'burst compute usage' but they are absent.
logs: Customer provided batch job manifest: job_id=qh-emb-20260202-0010, worker_pool=reserved-pool-phi-2, model=embed-multilingual-1, records=1,250,000, status=SUCCEEDED
Partial billing export from customer showing invoice lines: 'Reserved capacity adjustment -120h -$6,400' and no corresponding 'burst compute' lines for 2026-02-02
comments: 2026-02-10 Support (Maya): Opened ticket after call with QuantaHealth billing lead. Asked for job manifest, timestamps, and invoice PDF. QuantaHealth attached manifest and invoice PDF in thread.

2026-02-11 Finance (Priya Rao): Noted reserve credits are usually triggered by autoscaling reconciliation; asked Billing Team to confirm whether the reservation was marked 'unused' by reconciliation job on 2026-02-02.
2026-02-12 Engineering (Leo): Requested metering raw lines for pool 'reserved-pool-phi-2' for 2026-02-02 00:00–06:00 UTC and the autoscaler reconciliation logs for 2026-02-01 -> 2026-02-03 window.

2026-02-12 SRE (Diego): Uploaded paginator of metering lines: found a gap in ingestion between 2026-02-02 00:12 and 2026-02-02 01:05 UTC for pool 'reserved-pool-phi-2' due to transient metering pipeline backfill job failure (job backfill-20260202-1).

2026-02-13 Finance (Priya): Confirmed invoice generation job ran 2026-02-03 and used the reconciliation output from 2026-02-02 which flagged 120h as unused because of the ingestion gap. Asked Eng to provide a corrected metering export so we can reissue invoice adjustment.

2026-02-14 Customer (QuantaHealth - Alex G): Customer requests expedited credit reversal and corrected invoice PDF for internal cost allocation; also requested root cause and mitigation to prevent recurrence.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Metering gap caused autoscaler/billing-recon process to think reserved hours were unused and issued a reserve credit while batch run charges fell into the gap and were not attributed.

Metering pipeline logs indicate an ingestion error in shard-us-east-1-5 between 00:12 and 01:05 UTC; backfill job failed to mark some burst usage lines as committed due to a throttling exception on the ingestion API (429 from upstream).
Batch job qh-emb-20260202-0010 has completed and produced tokens/embeddings; runtime logs show request latencies normal and no retry storm, so client-side duplication unlikely.

Reconciliation logic: If a reservation shows zero consumed hours in the reconciliation window, a 'unused reservation rollover' credit is applied; that logic ran before the backfill completed, which explains credit application.
resolution_notes: Action 1 (Engineering): Triggered manual backfill for shard-us-east-1-5 covering 2026-02-02 00:00–06:00 UTC. Confirmed the metering backfill populated ~3,750 'burst compute' lines tied to qh-emb-20260202-0010 totaling 118 reserved hours consumed.

Action 2 (Billing): Re-ran reconciliation using backfilled metering export and generated an invoice adjustment reversing the -$6,400 reserve credit and adding a corrected burst usage charge of $6,250 (net delta -$150, due to rounding/prorate), created credit memo CM-20260214-512478.
Action 3 (Support): Sent corrected invoice PDF and credit memo to Alex G (QuantaHealth) on 2026-02-14 and scheduled a 1:1 to walk through changes and provide CSV of corrected charge lines.

Action 4 (SRE/Engineering): Root cause: transient 429 throttling in ingestion API due to a misconfigured autoscaling policy during a control-plane deploy. Mitigation: increased ingestion API concurrency limit for metering pipeline and added alert for ingestion gaps > 5 minutes. Follow-up ticket INT-33015 created to harden backfill retry logic.
Status: Awaiting Finance to confirm final invoice adjustment on customer account and for customer to confirm reconciliation on their side.
